main_text.p: sium in amœno eundem erexisse querceto, non inepta quorundam coniectura est, ex Genes. 12. v. 6. Vbi mentio fit אלון מורה[?], quæ si proprie verba interpreteris, quercum seu quercetum doctoris vel monstratoris indigitant.

Nempe diuinæ pariter & seculari professioni accommodatissimam elegit sedem, in qua ipsam Naturam quasi loquentem, & Conditoris Dei laudes prædicantem, inter arbores amœnissimas, audire ac videre discipuli poterant.

Scribit enim Braccardus quercetum hoc, seu conuallem quercubus consitam inter montes duos Gelboe & Hermon, per totum Iordanis defluxum, ad mare mortuum vsque excurrisse, admiranda loci amœnitate & pulchritudine, propter arbores, & vberrimas aquas, quibus, Paradisi instar, rigabatur & decorabatur.

Ab Abrahamo ad posteros ejus Scholarum & doctrinæ sanioris tam sacræ, quam secularis cura transiit: tandemque cum Iosepho in Ægyptum migravit, quæ annis LXXX tanti viri vsa conuersatione in Naturæ & Gratiæ penetralia ingerere se potuit. Iosepho Iosepho Moses successit, qui, vt Stephanus in Aposto-licis

page.notes: Right edge strip shows the neighbouring page and is excluded. The Hebrew words in the Genesis reference (אלון מורה) are uncertain as to vowel points and box-like print; marked [?]. The Iosepho and Moses marginal notes in the left margin are handwritten-looking and were read with some doubt; the "Moses" note stands beside "Iosepho Moses" in the text, and the "Iosepho" note beside "cum Iosepho". Underlining and linking marks in the text are not transcribed. The word "Aposto-licis" is split at the line end with a printed hyphen.
